root_cause.text: The isofs_export_iget() function only validated that the block number was non-zero, failing to check if the attacker-controlled block number from the NFS file handle was within the valid range of the filesystem (block < s_nzones), allowing arbitrary in-range blocks on the backing device to be read as iso_directory_record structures.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes the validation from `if (block == 0)` to `if (block == 0 || block >= ISOFS_SB(sb)->s_nzones)`, adding an upper bound check. The CVE description explicitly states that "isofs_fh_to_dentry() and isofs_fh_to_parent() pass an attacker-controlled block number (ifid->block or ifid->parent_block) from the NFS file handle to isofs_export_iget(), which only rejects block == 0 before calling isofs_iget() and ultimately sb_bread()" and that "A crafted file handle...can still drive the server to read any in-range block on the backing device as if it were an iso_directory_record."

intent_record.intent_summary: Add upper boundary validation for block parameter to prevent out-of-bounds zone access in isofs_export_iget().
intent_record.what: Added an additional boundary check condition to the if statement: changed `if (block == 0)` to `if (block == 0 || block >= ISOFS_SB(sb)->s_nzones)` to also validate that block does not exceed the maximum number of zones in the ISO9660 superblock.
intent_record.how: The function now rejects inode export requests not only when block is zero, but also when block exceeds or equals the superblock's s_nzones limit. This prevents out-of-bounds access to zone data structures and potential memory corruption or invalid inode lookups by catching invalid block numbers before they are passed to isofs_iget().
